findings.reason: §2 can pass every one of its measures with the grouping dimension it was sized for entirely untouched, leaving the plan's stated goal unowned.
findings.text: §2's endpoint ends at "the one definition and template", while the batches it applies carry the grouping axis on 1,384 of their 2,893 name placements and §1 reports 98 of 125 families diverging on `physics_domain` grouping; `sn edit` offers no domain mode (its `--axis` accepts only `name|docs|both`), and §5's done-when measures a name against its own stored decision rather than agreement across a family, so no section closes family-level grouping

findings.reason: the defect sn-catalog-grouping §3 that §5 carries forward is precisely disagreement between writers over one domain property, so §2 running first recreates it and §2 running second discards §5's repair.
findings.text: §2 changes `physics_domain` on 1,384 placements while §5 repairs the same property through the one writer, and neither section's depends-on nor followup f-scc-001's "§4 to §8 are independent of it and of each other" (plan.html:98) acknowledges the overlap

findings.reason: as written §2 cannot reach its done-when until a ruling obtained elsewhere lands, and a coordinator cannot order the two from the declarations.
findings.text: §2's done-when requires every sized batch applied, but two of the 279 batches are the lineage rename and the release-candidate advisory renames, whose survivor and treatment only §4's lead ruling and §3's post-run measure produce; neither §3 nor §4 declares a relationship to §2 in either direction

findings.reason: two plans consume one cap and neither reconciles the draws, so the pass can exhaust the budget the continuation run was approved against with no point at which anyone chose it.
findings.text: the only spend control is per batch, "a batch whose estimate exceeds USD 50 goes to the lead", but the sizing artifact's largest batch is USD 1.38 (25 names at the USD 0.055 rate) so the rule can never fire; the pass total of USD 159.12 is therefore never a lead decision, while sn-full-dd-continuation §4 draws its limit from the same USD 350 approval ("never larger than what remains"), of which sn-integrity-backlog §52 records USD 280 remaining and §1 rules the two workstreams concurrent

findings.reason: a ceiling derived from a documentation rate applied to review-priced work understates the spend it is meant to bound, and §2's done-when requires spend recorded beside an estimate that measures a different operation.
findings.text: each batch's ceiling is its "sized estimate plus a quarter", but the sizing artifact states its cost is "the measured documentation rate of $0.055 per name", whereas §2's work is `sn edit`, which rides the generate→review→score pipeline (its inline review carries its own `--cost-limit`, default USD 1.0)

findings.reason: a count taken beside a name-creating run can fall or rise without the pass changing anything, so the measure cannot tell a good pass from a bad one.
findings.text: §2 compares absolute counts against the 2026-11-10 reading of 125 and 91 and, at plan.html:53, requires the sourceless-draft count not to rise, while §1's lead ruling lets the batches run before or beside the full-DD continuation, whose §4 targets 300 new accepted names entering the same families; §3 has the escape clause §2 lacks ("any family the run newly made divergent is either applied … or listed with its reason", plan.html:62)

findings.reason: a read-back never shown to fire cannot distinguish a repaired catalogue from a query that returns nothing whatever the graph holds.
findings.text: §4 closes on "the lineage census reports one live tip for this lineage and no new cycle", and §7 at plan.html:85 closes on a live read-back listing no sourceless name, and neither declares a planted case; §2, §3, §5 and §8 each declare one (a planted divergent family, a planted dangling link, a planted disagreeing name, the census's planted control)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — sn-integrity-backlog §52, §49, §46 and §22, sn-catalog-grouping §3 and sn-full-dd-continuation §4 all exist in this tree, both cited fragment JSONs exist, and every number §1 cites reproduces against the census JSON (3,034 names, 130 families, 125 divergent, 98/98/98 per dimension, 91 concepts, 25 variants over 25 members).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2 compares absolute census counts (125 divergent families, 91 concepts, and a sourceless-draft count that must not rise) taken while the DD continuation run creates new names beside it (plan.html:50, 53); §4 and §7 name no negative control for the read-back they close on (plan.html:70, 85).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the census and batches evidence resolve at docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-consistency-census.json and sib-consistency-batches.json, and the section gates report library instruments (the census re-run, the domain audit, the export dry run) rather than a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the plan names no code symbol, file or function for a worker to implement, and carries no plan label, ticket number or version tag into a name.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the plan's own goal ("one grouping", plan.html:33) is not closed by any section: §2's endpoint is "one definition and template" (plan.html:44) and §5's done-when only makes each name agree with its own stored decision (plan.html:75), which one family with ten different decisions satisfies.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 through §8 each name one deliverable (the batches applied, the cut clean, one live tip, domains agreeing, one suffix, no sourceless name, the chain-cap re-measure) and their gates judge that deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §2's done-when requires every sized batch applied, including the lineage and unit-pair rename batches whose survivor/ruling only §4 and §3 can obtain, and no depends-on or ordering is declared between §2, §3 and §4 (plan.html:48, 69, 98); §2 and §5 also both write `physics_domain` over overlapping names with no declared relationship (plan.html:44, 75).
